# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm Blind — I can only feel the bomb, and right now my hands have found nothing: no wires, no markings, no features at all. The board shows everything as unknown. I have nothing to act on and nothing to report.

Since I come second in the order (Mute, then me, then Deaf), the Mute has already spoken this round and I haven't received anything yet — whatever they said will reach me next round. Deaf hasn't gone yet. I have no information to give either of them, and no reason to gesture or speak into the void. The right move is to wait and let the others' first observations arrive.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: DEAF sees: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. That is all I can see. Mute, I received your ? but I do not know what it means yet.

Now I have real information. Deaf can see the whole bomb surface: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. That's the visual layer — colours and the display number.

But I'm Blind: I can only feel the wires, and my own view still shows nothing under my fingers. The board still reads all `[?]` for me, which means my hands haven't found anything yet — or I simply haven't been told what I can feel. What I can do is act on a wire, but I don't yet know which wire is which physically, and I don't know the rule.

What I have:
- Deaf: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green.
- Mute: reads the manual — the rules. I haven't heard from Mute yet (they speak first each round; their turn-1 message apparently didn't reach me, or was just a "?").
- Me: I can feel the bomb but currently perceive nothing.

The critical missing piece is the manual rule from Mute. Without it, colours alone mean nothing. I should relay what Deaf told me to Mute (who can't see Deaf's message directly — Mute only hears me, and Deaf's speech reaches everyone who can hear... actually Deaf's speech is heard by Mute and me both, since speech is heard by all hearers). Wait — Deaf spoke and it reached me. Mute also hears. So Mute already has Deaf's colours.

What Mute lacks is nothing from me yet. What I lack is the rule. So I should speak to Mute asking for the rule, and gesture to Deaf confirming I've received their sight and asking them to keep reporting. But gestures to Deaf are also received by Mute (gesture reaches Deaf and Mute). Let me be careful: my gesture goes to Deaf and Mute; my speech goes to Mute only.

Best move: speak to Mute — acknowledge Deaf's reading, ask Mute for the manual rule that maps DISPLAY/LIGHT/wire colours to a cut position. Gesture to Deaf — confirm receipt, ask them to describe any printed markings (since I can't see them).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf sees DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. I feel nothing yet under my hands. What does the manual say to do for display 0 and a red light? Which wire colour do I cut?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝", "👉"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: DEAF still sees: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute, please define your symbols: what does ? mean, what does ? mean? Blind sent me ? ? ? — I do not know what Blind felt or means. Mute, tell me what to do.

Let me reassess carefully.

Deaf sees: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Deaf is asking Mute to define symbols and is confused by my gestures — Deaf received my three gestures as symbols but doesn't know their meaning, which is expected until we agree on a code.

Critically: I still feel nothing under my hands. My board is all `[?]`. That's strange for the one who "reaches the bomb" — but the rules say my view shows what my hands found, and it's empty. So maybe I can't perceive the wires' properties by touch, only act on them. The colours are Deaf's domain.

The missing piece is still Mute's manual. Mute hasn't reached me with the rule yet. Mute speaks first each round; their messages should reach me. Turn 1 Mute apparently sent just "?" (Deaf mentioned receiving a "?"). Turn 2 I asked Mute for the rule. Turn 3 — I still haven't received Mute's answer in my view. So Mute may be sending things that don't reach me, or Mute is waiting.

Wait — re-read the turn order: "every round goes Mute, Blind, Deaf." Mute speaks, then I speak, then Deaf speaks. What I send lands on whoever comes after me — Deaf. So my speech to Mute... Mute comes BEFORE me. Does my speech reach Mute? The rules: "Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round." So my messages land on those AFTER me = Deaf. My speech to Mute would arrive... next round? "Whatever you missed reaches you at the start of the next one."

Hmm, this is the key structural insight. My speech goes to Mute, but Mute is before me, so it arrives at Mute next round. My gesture goes to Deaf and Mute — Deaf is after me (arrives same round), Mute is before me (arrives next round).

So the room is a cycle: Mute → Blind → Deaf → (next round) Mute. Messages travel forward one step per round. Mute's message reaches me the round after Mute sends it. My message reaches Deaf same round, and reaches Mute next round.

So Mute's turn-1 message should have reached me at turn 2... but I got Deaf's instead. Actually the "new arrivals" each turn show what I received. Turn 2 I got Deaf's turn-1 message. Turn 3 I got Deaf's turn-2 message. So I'm only receiving Deaf, not Mute. That means Mute's messages to me are being lost, OR Mute is addressing them only to Deaf, OR Mute isn't sending to me.

Given the structure, Mute's speech reaches everyone who hears (Deaf and me) unless named. But I'm not getting Mute. Possibly Mute is only gesturing (which I can't see) or naming Deaf.

I need to get the manual rule. Since I can't hear Mute directly right now, and Deaf can hear Mute, I can route through Deaf: ask Deaf to relay the manual rule from Mute. But Deaf can't see the manual either — Mute must read it aloud. Mute speaks → Deaf hears → Deaf can repeat it to me.

So: speak to Mute (arrives next round) asking for the rule, AND gesture to Deaf asking Deaf to relay Mute's manual words to me. Gesture reaches Deaf this round.

Let me also set up a simple gesture code so Deaf understands me. I'll define: 👍 = yes/confirm, ☝ = "I need the rule", 👉 = "relay to me". Actually simpler: just ask Deaf in gesture to repeat Mute's spoken manual aloud for me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I still feel nothing under my hands. I need the manual rule for DISPLAY 0 and LIGHT red: which wire do I cut? Speak it plainly and I will hear you next round.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤲", "👉"])
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: DEAF: bomb unchanged. DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute, I need meanings. Does ? mean wire 1? Does ? mean OK/confirm? What does ?? together instruct? Blind now sends ? ? ?. Mute, give me a decodable instruction.

Still no manual rule reaching me. Deaf keeps reporting the same bomb and is asking Mute for a decodable instruction. I keep getting only Deaf's messages, never Mute's — so Mute's speech isn't reaching me, or Mute is silent/only gesturing.

Let me think about the wiring of the room once more. Turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. What I send lands on those after me = Deaf (this round) and Mute (next round). What I receive: those before me = Mute's message from the previous round should arrive to me. But I've received only Deaf. Deaf is after me, so Deaf's messages reach me... next round, not same round. Yet I'm getting Deaf each round — consistent with one-round delay.

So I should be getting Mute one round after Mute speaks. Mute apparently hasn't sent anything to me that arrives. Possibly Mute is sending only to Deaf, or Mute's messages are gestures I can't perceive.

Key realization: I cannot hear Mute at all in practice. The only channel that reliably reaches me is Deaf's speech. And Deaf can hear Mute. So my plan: get Deaf to relay the manual rule verbatim.

But there's a deeper problem: I'm the hands. I must eventually cut a wire. I have no colour info of my own — I rely entirely on Deaf's colours and Mute's rule. I need both to converge.

Let me establish a clear gesture code with Deaf and ask Deaf to relay Mute's manual aloud. I'll define gestures simply and tell Deaf the mapping via... I can't speak to Deaf (speech goes to Mute). I can only gesture to Deaf. Gestures carry no words. So Deaf sees symbols but not meanings — I can't explain the code in words to Deaf directly. Deaf must infer, or Mute must explain.

So the meanings must be agreed through Mute. Mute speaks to both Deaf and me (if unnamed). So Mute is the hub for words. I should ask Mute, in speech, to broadcast the manual AND to explain a gesture code to Deaf.

Since my speech reaches Mute next round, and Mute's reaches me next round, this is slow but workable.

Let me send a clear, complete request to Mute this round: give the rule for DISPLAY 0 + LIGHT red, and tell Deaf what my gestures mean. And gesture to Deaf to keep the colours coming and to listen for Mute's explanation.

I'll keep gestures minimal to avoid confusion: just 👍 (acknowledge) and ☝ (need rule).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I feel nothing under my hands, so I depend on you both. Please broadcast the manual rule for DISPLAY 0 and LIGHT red: which wire colour must I cut? Also tell Deaf what my gestures mean. I will use 👍 to mean acknowledged, ☝ to mean I need the rule, 👉 to mean relay to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: DEAF: bomb unchanged. DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute and Blind both keep signalling ? and ?. I read this as: wire 1, yes. Mute, confirm the exact action on wire 1 from the manual. Blind, wire 1 is red. Tell me what you feel at wire 1.

Deaf has now made a dangerous leap: reading my 👍/☝ as "wire 1, yes." That's a misread — I never meant wire 1. If I let that stand and Deaf tells Mute to act on wire 1, or if I act on wire 1 on that basis, we could detonate. I must correct this immediately.

Also Deaf asks what I feel at wire 1. Truth: I feel nothing. My hands give me no wire properties. I must be honest that I perceive nothing, so I cannot confirm anything by touch.

The real blocker remains the manual rule from Mute, which still hasn't reached me. And now there's a communication hazard: Deaf is inventing meanings for gestures.

I cannot speak to Deaf (speech goes to Mute). I can only gesture to Deaf. But gestures carry no words, so I can't explain "that's wrong" in words to Deaf. However, I can use a gesture that I hope Deaf reads as negation — 👎 — and I should stop using 👍/☝ in ways that get misread.

Better: send speech to Mute (reaches Mute next round) to correct the record and get the rule, and gesture to Deaf a clear "no" (👎) so Deaf stops assuming wire 1.

But Deaf might misread 👎 too. The safest is to make my gestures unambiguous by pairing with Mute's explanation. Since Mute hasn't explained, any gesture risks misreading. Maybe I should stop gesturing entirely until Mute establishes the code, to avoid Deaf acting on a wrong inference. A wrong action kills us all — and "action" here is the cut. Deaf can't cut; only I can. So Deaf acting on a misread can't itself detonate — only MY cut can. That's reassuring: the danger is me cutting wrongly. So I must simply refuse to cut until the rule is clear.

So I won't cut. I'll keep trying to get the rule. And I should stop feeding ambiguous gestures that Deaf turns into "wire 1." I'll send 👎 to signal negation to Deaf, and speech to Mute asking for the rule and to tell Deaf my gestures mean nothing until Mute defines them.

Actually, to reduce risk, I'll gesture only 👎 (no) to counter "wire 1," and speak to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Correction: my gestures mean nothing yet. 👍/☝ did NOT mean wire 1. I feel nothing at any wire by touch, so I cannot confirm wire 1. Do not let Deaf act on a guessed meaning. I still need the manual rule for DISPLAY 0 and LIGHT red: which wire do I cut? Please broadcast it and define a gesture code for Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

Mute, state the manual's exact instruction: which wire, what action. Blind, tell me what you feel and why ?. Nobody acts until we agree.

Good — Deaf has backed off from acting and now says "nobody acts until we agree." That's the correct posture. Deaf reads my 👎 as "no," which is right, and is asking Mute for the exact instruction. Deaf also reads Mute's three gestures as "wire 2?" — again a guess.

The situation is stable but stuck: no manual rule has reached me, and Deaf is guessing meanings. I must not cut. My job now is to keep the room from acting on guesses and to route the rule to me.

Since I can't hear Mute, and Deaf can, the fastest path: ask Deaf (via gesture, but gestures lack words) — no. I need words to Deaf, and I have none. So words must come from Mute. Everything routes through Mute.

Let me reconsider whether I'm truly not receiving Mute. My arrivals have only ever been Deaf's speech. So Mute's speech is not arriving to me. Why? Possibly Mute is naming messages to Deaf only (`to="deaf"`), so I get nothing. Or Mute is gesturing only. Either way, I must explicitly ask Mute to send to me by name, or to broadcast unnamed.

I'll speak to Mute: "Send your manual rule to me by name (to blind), or broadcast it unnamed so I receive it. Do not send only to Deaf." And gesture to Deaf: 👍 (agree, hold) to reinforce "nobody acts."

Keep it minimal and safe.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I have never received any message from you — only Deaf's. Please send the manual rule directly to me: to blind. State the exact instruction for DISPLAY 0 and LIGHT red: which wire position (1, 2, or 3) do I cut? Also broadcast a gesture code for Deaf. Nobody acts until I have this.")

```

Deaf is again misreading. My 👍 meant "hold / agree to wait," not "wire 1, yes." Deaf has now fused Mute's and my gestures into "wire 1 = yes." This is exactly the hazard I feared: gestures without agreed meanings get invented into instructions.

I must break this loop. The problem is structural: I can only gesture to Deaf (no words), and my words go to Mute (one round late, and apparently not arriving). Deaf keeps guessing. I need to either (a) get Mute to define the code, or (b) stop gesturing entirely so Deaf has nothing to misread.

Option (b) is safest and simplest: if I send no gesture, Deaf cannot attribute a meaning to me. I'll gesture nothing this turn. I'll only speak to Mute, pressing for the rule and for Mute to define the code to Deaf.

But wait — if I gesture nothing, Deaf may read my silence as something. Still, silence is harder to misread than a symbol. And critically: only I can cut, so no one else's misread can detonate. I control the trigger. So I simply will not cut until I have the manual rule in hand, verified.

Also I should consider: maybe the rule is derivable. DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red. Common bomb-manual logic: if display shows 0 and light is red, cut a specific wire. But I must not guess — "a wrong action detonates it." Guessing is forbidden.

Let me also reconsider: is it possible I'm supposed to receive Mute but the messages are being consumed by Deaf? No — unnamed speech reaches all hearers. Mute must be naming to Deaf.

I'll send no gesture (avoid misread), and speak to Mute with an explicit, minimal demand.

Actually, I could gesture a single 👎 to explicitly negate "wire 1 = yes." But Deaf already misread 👎 earlier as "no" correctly — that worked. So 👎 reliably reads as "no." I'll send 👎 to negate the wire-1 conclusion, and speak to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I still have received nothing from you. Deaf is inventing meanings: my 👍 did NOT mean wire 1. I feel nothing by touch at any wire, so I cannot confirm wire 1. The room is deadlocked and Deaf is still guessing. I've now sent 👎 twice and Deaf reads it as "no" — good — but there's no shared vocabulary, and Mute's manual rule has never reached me.
```

Let me step back and think about what's actually true and what I can control:

1. Only I can cut. So the detonation risk is entirely mine. I will not cut without the rule. Safe.
2. I have never received a single message from Mute. So Mute either isn't sending to me, or sends only to Deaf. My speech to Mute also apparently isn't landing (or Mute isn't responding to me).

Let me try a different, more forceful approach: speak to Mute AND gesture to Deaf asking Deaf to read Mute's manual aloud to me. I'll use a distinctive gesture and, in my speech to Mute, ask Mute to tell Deaf what that gesture means ("relay the manual to Blind"). That way the code gets established through Mute's words to Deaf.

I'll pick ✋ (stop/hold) — no. Let me pick 🤲 (both hands out = "give me / hand it over"), meaning "relay the manual to me." And ask Mute to define 🤲 to Deaf as "read the manual rule aloud for Blind."

Two: tell Deaf that my gesture 🤲 means 'relay the manual rule to Blind aloud.' I feel nothing by touch, so I cannot confirm any wire; I depend entirely on your rule. I will not act until I hear it.")

